title: Ionization energies; Periodic table structure and blocks
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: PT01#t1 term and clue written for the game; PT01#t3 term and clue written for the game; AS05#t3 term and clue written for the game; PT01#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: AS05#N.4b, PT01#N.6, AS05#N.10b, PT01#N.10, AS05#N.11, PT01#N.12a.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Period
items.clue: A row of the table; its number gives the outer occupied shell.

items.label: Valence electrons
items.clue: The outer-shell particles of an atom: seven for bromine, 4s² 4p⁵.

items.label: Convergence limit
items.clue: Where hydrogen's lines for falls to n = 1 crowd together at high frequency.

items.label: Metalloid
items.clue: Element on the stepped line, such as B, Si or Ge, with in-between properties.

questions.stem: Which statement describes the process whose energy change is the first ionization energy of magnesium?

options.text: An atom in solid Mg loses two electrons, forming an aqueous Mg²⁺ ion
An atom in solid Mg loses one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁺ ion
A gaseous Mg atom takes in one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁻ ion
A gaseous Mg atom loses one electron, forming a gaseous Mg⁺ ion

questions.explanation: One electron removed from an isolated gaseous atom in its ground state.

questions.stem: Germanium is in period 4, group 14. Which is the full electron configuration of a germanium atom?

options.text: 1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 4s² 4p²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d² 4s²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p²
1s² 2s² 2p⁶ 3s² 3p⁶ 3d¹⁰ 4s² 4p⁴

questions.explanation: Period 4, p-block: fill up to 4p. Group 14 gives 14 − 10 = 4 valence electrons, 4s² 4p². With the 3d¹⁰, the total is 32 electrons.

questions.stem: The first four ionization energies of an element in period 3 are 496, 4562, 6910 and 9543 kJ/mol. Which element is it?

options.text: Al, because three electrons are removed after the large jump
Na, because one electron is removed before the large jump
Mg, because the second value is the first one above 1000 kJ/mol
Ar, because a noble gas needs the most energy to ionize

questions.explanation: The second value is about nine times the first: one valence electron, then the core. Group 1, period 3: sodium.

questions.stem: An element has the ground-state electron configuration 1s²2s²2p⁶3s²3p⁴. What is the typical charge of the ions of this element in its ionic compounds?
questions.explanation: The atom has six valence electrons, 3s²3p⁴. It gains two electrons, giving a valence shell of eight and two more electrons than protons: a charge of −2, as in sulfide.

questions.stem: Element X is in Period 3. Its first six ionization energies are 1012, 1907, 2914, 4964, 6274 and 21 268 kJ/mol. Which statement identifies X and explains the large sixth value?

options.text: X is sulfur: the jump is at the sixth ionisation energy, so X has six outer electrons.
X is phosphorus: the sixth electron is the first from the second shell, nearer the nucleus.
X is phosphorus: the sixth electron would come from a full shell, which is especially stable.
X is aluminium: the rise from 2914 to 4964 is where a new shell starts.

questions.explanation: Five electrons come from the third shell. The sixth comes from 2p: much closer to the nucleus, much less shielded, so held far more strongly.

questions.stem: Beryllium, 1s² 2s², and helium, 1s², both have two electrons in their outer s sub-shell. Why is beryllium placed in group 2, but helium in group 18?

options.text: Beryllium is a solid and helium is a gas, and group 18 holds the gaseous elements.
Beryllium has four electrons and helium two, and the group number counts the total.
Beryllium's 2s² electrons are in a higher shell, so they are inner electrons, not valence electrons.
Beryllium's outer shell, n = 2, is far from full, while helium's n = 1 shell is full with just two.
